classification.difficultyReason: Choose a line balancing the scattered points, judge correlation strength and use the constructed line to estimate either height from the other.

content.prompt: The scatterplot shows a mother’s height and her daughter’s height.

spec.description: Ten points and a square grid for drawing a line of best fit. Point positions are traced approximations, not an exact dataset. No answer line appears in the question graph.
spec.mathematics: Both axes run from 150 to 180 cm; labelled ticks occur every 10 cm, grid lines every 2.5 cm and finer unlabelled ticks every 2 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The student draws directly on this graph; the example answer line is solution-only.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a line of best fit.

answer.short: An upward-sloping line through the centre of the points; see the example. Other reasonable lines are acceptable.
answer.worked: Draw a straight line through the centre of the scatter, with roughly equal numbers of points above and below it. One acceptable example passes through approximately (154, 162) and (170, 172).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Describe the strength of the relationship as strong, moderate, or weak.

answer.worked: Moderate: the points follow an upward trend but have noticeable scatter about a line of best fit.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Estimate the daughter’s height if the mother’s height is 170 cm.

answer.short: About 172 cm; reasonable estimates depend on the line drawn.
answer.worked: From 170 cm on the mother’s-height axis, read up to your line and across to the daughter’s-height axis. The example line gives about 172 cm; another reasonable line may give a slightly different estimate.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Estimate the mother’s height if the daughter’s height is 162 cm.

answer.short: About 154 cm; reasonable estimates depend on the line drawn.
answer.worked: From 162 cm on the daughter’s-height axis, read across to your line and down to the mother’s-height axis. The example line gives about 154 cm; another reasonable line may give a slightly different estimate.

spec.description: Complete source graph with one acceptable authored by-eye line. Other reasonable lines and corresponding estimates are acceptable.
spec.mathematics: Example line passes through approximately (154,162) and (170,172), supporting the source estimates without imposing a unique regression line.
